# Using X Research in GitHub Copilot

<!-- Generated by `node packages/cli build` from the harness registry. Do not edit by hand. -->

The skill is the same in every agent. This guide covers only what is specific to GitHub Copilot.

## Install

Project scope (one repository): copy this skill folder to `.github/skills/x-research/`.

User scope (every project): copy it to `~/.copilot/skills/x-research/`.

From the gti-skills repository, the CLI does the copy for you:

```bash
node packages/cli install --harness copilot --skill x-research
node packages/cli install --harness copilot --skill x-research --scope user
```

Restart the agent session after installing so it rescans its skills.

## Use

Describe the task in plain language. GitHub Copilot loads the skill when the request matches its `description`. You can also name it in the request, for example: "Use the x-research skill to ...".

## Where the skill finds its files

`<skill-dir>` in `SKILL.md` is the folder that contains `SKILL.md`: `.github/skills/x-research` for a project install, or `~/.copilot/skills/x-research` for a user install. Scripts and references are always addressed relative to it.

## Verify

Ask the agent which skills it has loaded and check that `x-research` is listed.

## Notes

- Copilot also reads .claude/skills and .agents/skills. Works in VS Code agent mode, Copilot CLI, and the cloud agent.
- This skill calls the twitter MCP server in packages/python/twitter-mcp. Register that server in this agent and log in once with its login.py before using the skill.
- Documentation: [GitHub Copilot](https://docs.github.com/en/copilot/how-tos/use-copilot-agents/cloud-agent/create-skills) (path source: official).
